newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti chief optimistic for rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti chief optimistic for rescue plan.

text.p: Olivetti chief executive Roberto Colaninno said he was confident about the success of a restructuring plan for the troubled high-tech group.

He said he was sure the plan, which envisages a string of sell-offs in 1996 and 1997 including that of its loss-making PC company, "can contribute relatively rapidly to the financial re-equilibrium of the group and provide resources for the development of strategic areas."
Colaninno was speaking to the industry commission of the upper house of parliament, the Senate.
Despite the difficult financial situation, he said he was "convinced the group could face up to the current problems and bring its strategic plan to its conclusion."
"In the meetings I have had in recent days the financial world has confirmed to me its confidence in Olivetti's recovery," he added.

Colaninno met analysts in Milan and London last week, his first presentation to the financial community since his appointment last month to replace Francesco Caio, who was forced out of the company within three months of taking the helm.
He told the Senate commission Olivetti aimed to "confront the challenge with its own resources without falling back on extraordinary state intervention."
For this reason he had had to think of giving up "activities which are not part of the core business of the future Olivetti," he added. -- Milan newsroom +392 66129589
